$comment: Request/response JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for madlad.postman_collection.json, rendered into its items' descriptions and MADLAD_SCHEMAS.md (linked from MADLAD.md). Edit here, then: uv run --no-sync python scripts/api_schemas.py render. Hand-written from api/madlad_server.py (madlad-api) and app/app.py (madlad-app, whose /languages and /translate bodies madlad-api passes through); checked by unit-tests/apidocs only (there is no in-process harness). The MCP envelope follows the MCP SDK's models (open objects) as FastMCP 3.4.5 fills them; madlad-api's image resolves fastmcp>=2.0 at build time.

mcp_initialize_params.$comment: mcp.types.InitializeRequestParams: the SDK allows extra keys

protocolVersion.description: The latest version of the Model Context Protocol that the client supports

mcp_initialize_result.$comment: mcp.types.InitializeResult: the SDK allows extra keys

protocolVersion.description: The version of the Model Context Protocol that the server wants to use; it may not match the version the client requested

capabilities.description: What the server supports (`mcp.types.ServerCapabilities`); FastMCP announces `tools`, `prompts`, `resources` and `logging`

cursor.description: An opaque token representing the current pagination position

200.description: madlad-api is up; madlad-app is not checked

GET /v1/madlad/languages.description: madlad-app's body, passed through. Any madlad-app failure -- unreachable, or an error status of its own -- is a 502 `{"detail": "Cannot reach madlad-app: …"}`.

languages.description: Every target language the checkpoint's tokenizer has a `<2xx>` token for, sorted by code

code.description: Used as `target_lang` in /translate. ISO 639-1 where available, otherwise ISO 639-3, occasionally with a regional suffix (e.g. `zh_CN`)

name.description: Resolved via the `langcodes` library; an unknown code falls back to the code itself

POST /v1/madlad/translate.description: madlad-app's body, passed through. Any madlad-app failure is a 502 `{"detail": "Cannot reach madlad-app: …"}` -- an unknown `target_lang` too (madlad-app's own 400), and a model that produced nothing (its 500).

text.description: Source language is auto-detected; there is no `src` field

target_lang.description: One of the codes GET /languages returns

MCP initialize.description: The JSON-RPC response's `result` (streamable HTTP at `/mcp/`: one SSE `data:` message when the request accepts `text/event-stream`); the `mcp-session-id` response header names the session the later calls send back.

result.$comment: mcp.types.ListToolsResult: the SDK allows extra keys

items.$comment: mcp.types.Tool: the SDK allows extra keys

description.description: The tool's docstring summary: what the model reads

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema: the arguments of `MCP translate`

outputSchema.description: A JSON Schema of `structuredContent`: `{"result": <string>}` (FastMCP wraps a `str` return)

MCP translate.description: The JSON-RPC response's `result.structuredContent` (one SSE `data:` message); `result.content[0].text` carries the same string. A madlad-app failure is not a tool error: it comes back as the string.

arguments.$comment: translate(text: str, target_lang: str) as FastMCP 3.4.5 lists it (it closes a tool's arguments)

text.description: The source text. Source language is auto-detected.

target_lang.description:
ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. "es", "fr", "ja", "zh").
Call the /languages endpoint for the full list of supported codes.

result.description: The translated text; `Error translating: <httpx error>` when madlad-app cannot be reached or answers an error status (an unknown target_lang included). FastMCP wraps a `str` return as `{"result": …}`
